type_algebra.collection_semantics: Set values are unique and order-independent; List values preserve multiplicity and order

nodes.meaning: Server-side code that constructs the required permission, scope evidence, decision time, and authorization revision.
One trusted internal question naming a session and exact required permission.
One server-recognized session with status, expiry, authorization revision, and active role identities.
One authoritative role definition containing positive exact-match permission grants.
One exact resource, action, and scope triple.
Evidence that trusted application code constructed the required scope.
The authoritative revision shared by the request, session, and role relation.
Exactly ALLOW or DENY; diagnostic denial reasons are non-normative.
The complete trusted, already-resolved input presented to the pure authorization decision.
The current server-side lifecycle state of a resolved session.
A non-normative diagnostic classification for a DENY result.

rules.statement: The request must resolve to exactly one server-recognized session.
rules.failure_behavior: DENY with missing or ambiguous session diagnostics.

rules.statement: The session is ACTIVE, decision time is strictly before expiry, and its authorization revision equals the current request revision.
Trusted application code, not the external caller, constructed the required scope and supplied evidence of that construction.
Resolved roles contain every and only active role identity exactly once at the current authorization revision.
rules.failure_behavior: DENY; incomplete role data is never interpreted as an empty current grant set.

rules.statement: Authorization is admissible only when unique resolution, currentness, trusted scope evidence, and complete active-role resolution all hold.
At least one resolved active role grants a permission whose resource, action, and scope exactly equal the required permission.
Return ALLOW if and only if authorization is admissible and an exact active-role grant exists.
Every other in-scope result is DENY.

proof_requirements.statement: The binary decision is characterized by authorization evidence in both directions.
An admissible request with an exact active-role grant is allowed.
An admissible request without an exact active-role grant is denied.
A request without an admissible session context is denied.
A mismatch in resource, action, or scope is denied.
The Rust kernel returns ALLOW exactly for the ontology authorization-evidence predicate and DENY otherwise.

residue.description: Production session, role, revision, and scope-evidence resolvers remain external.
HTTP, persistence, tokens, and audit transport are outside the pure kernel.
The integrated service requires independent threat modeling and security review.

claim_limit: Proposed capability-local ontology for the exact accepted Auth rule; no runtime, deployment, or production-security authority.
